walkthroughs.body_html:
The Carbon Cycle & Energy Security — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Carbon Cycle & Energy Security brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Carbon Cycle & Energy Security.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was Russia's share of EU gas pre-2022?
How do humans affect the carbon cycle?
options: By burning fossil fuels (releasing stored geological carbon to the atmosphere) and deforestation (reducing the biosphere store and releasing carbon).
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
Humans only affect the carbon cycle by breathing out CO2.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
